preconditions.expression: 3 <= int(n) <= 10**5 and 0 <= int(m) <= 10**5 and 1 <= int(v) <= int(n)
preconditions.description: Input must satisfy 3 ≤ n ≤ 10^5, 0 ≤ m ≤ 10^5, and 1 ≤ v ≤ n, where n is the number of servers, m is the number of connections, and v is the failing server index.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= int(n) for x in stdin.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All server indices in input are within the valid range [1, n].

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdout.splitlines()) and len(stdout.splitlines()) == int(m))
postconditions.description: If no valid configuration exists, output is '-1'. Otherwise, output consists of exactly m lines, each containing two distinct server indices representing a connection.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and all(1 <= int(u) <= int(n) and 1 <= int(w) <= int(n) and u != w for line in stdout.splitlines() for u, w in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: Each connection in the output is between two distinct servers within the valid range [1, n].

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and any(all(int(u) != int(v) and int(w) != int(v) for u, w in [line.split()]) for line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: The failing server v is not directly connected to any other server in the output (i.e., v is isolated in the graph).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and (lambda: any(not all(int(u) in {int(x) for line in stdout.splitlines() for x in line.split()} for u in range(1, int(n)+1) if u != int(v))))()
postconditions.description: The graph is connected when server v is removed (i.e., the system is connected except for v).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and (lambda: all(int(u) != int(w) for line in stdout.splitlines() for u, w in [line.split()]))
postconditions.description: No duplicate connections exist in the output.
